subject: Coding Agent Benchmarks: Are We Measuring the Right Things?
body:
Hello First Name,

This week's 🦄 ai that works session tackled a big question: "Coding Agent Benchmarks: Are We Measuring the Right Things?"

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot about how coding agent benchmarks have evolved and where they stand today. Here's a quick recap:

*   **Benchmarks: Then and Now.** Early benchmarks, like Sweep Bench and Program Bench, usually focused on short-term outcomes, like solving a single problem. But things are getting better! Newer benchmarks, such as Frontier Code, include longer tasks and black-box testing. They even use judge models to check code quality and how well agents write their own tests.
*   **The Missing Piece: Real-World Maintenance.** Even with these improvements, current benchmarks still miss a big part of the picture. They struggle to truly evaluate an agent's ability to maintain and evolve a codebase over time. Can an agent adapt to unknown future requirements? Can it make smart architectural decisions that prevent 'sloppy' code and long-term issues? These are the real challenges.

If you have any questions, just reply to this email or ask on Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We read every message! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
